userStories.title: Vitest detection reads only test.include
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix M15 so Vitest and Vite detection never use a nested include as the test-file pattern.

**Motivation** — `parseViteConfig` extracts the `test: {}` block first but then runs the same regex inside it, so `coverage.include` written before `include` in that block wins there too.

**Approach** — `parseVitestConfig(workdir)` and `parseViteConfig(workdir)` (file-local, `framework-configs.ts:45`, `:281`).
Baseline: vitest matches `include` over the whole file; vite matches the first `include` anywhere inside the `test: {}` block. Target: both extract the `test: {}` block with `extractBalancedBlock` and read only an `include` key at the top level of the slice `extractBalancedBlock` returns (outside every nested `{}` in that slice), through one new file-local helper. `extractBalancedBlock` is unchanged; like it, the helper counts braces without regard to string literals. A vitest config with no `test` block, or with a `test` block that has no top-level `include`, returns the vitest source with `patterns: []` (it still claims the framework, as today).

`extractBalancedBlock(text: string, anchor: RegExp): string | null` — `src/test-runners/detect/framework-configs.ts:344`, file-local.
`extractStringLiterals` and `normalize(patterns: string[]): string[]` — same file, file-local.
`detectTestFilePatterns(workdir)` — `src/test-runners/detect/index.ts`; returns `{ patterns, confidence, sources }`. It drops sources with empty `patterns` (`index.ts:148-149`), so a vitest source with `patterns: []` is visible only through `detectFromFrameworkConfigs`.
`detectFromFrameworkConfigs(workdir): Promise<DetectionSource[]>` — `framework-configs.ts:367`, exported; returns every Tier 1 source, including one with `patterns: []`.

**Scope** — In: the two file-local parsers, one shared depth-aware include helper and new focused tests. Out: shared rule brace matching (US-002), scan caps (US-003), package validation (US-004), reserved names (US-005), process signaling (US-006) and publishing (US-007). Vitest configs whose `test.include` is not a literal string array (a variable, a spread, a function call). They keep returning `patterns: []`. Braces inside string literals in a vitest or vite config (for example `exclude: ["a/}"]`). They are counted as structure, as `extractBalancedBlock` counts them today. Vitest `test.projects` / workspace entries and an `alias` or other object holding a `test:` key before the config's own `test` block. Only the first `test: {` block's top-level `include` is read.

**Interface**
```ts
extractBalancedBlock(text: string, anchor: RegExp): string | null
normalize(patterns: string[]): string[]
detectFromFrameworkConfigs(workdir): Promise<DetectionSource[]>
```
These existing helpers/detectors retain their visibility; the new include helper stays file-local. Add `packages/nax/test/unit/test-runners/detect/framework-configs-vitest.test.ts` rather than growing the 612-line detect.test.ts. ACs on detectTestFilePatterns copy its _frameworkDefaultsDeps.readText and _fileScanDeps.spawn stubs and cache isolation (detect.test.ts:94-109).

userStories.title: Brace globs match in rule selection, attribution and lint
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix M16 by implementing brace alternation in the shared scope matcher and aligning rules lint with runtime.

**Motivation** — `SCOPE_GLOB_META` counts `{` as glob syntax, so `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` is compiled as a glob that matches only the literal text `*.{ts,tsx}`.

**Approach** — `globToRegex(pattern: string): RegExp` (`scope-path-match/index.ts:82`).
Baseline: escapes `{`, `}` and `,`. Target: a balanced brace group that contains at least one top-level `,` compiles to a non-capturing alternation — `{` to `(?:`, each top-level `,` inside the group to `|`, `}` to `)` — with nesting; `*`, `**` and `?` inside a group keep their meaning, and every other character inside a group stays regex-escaped as today. An empty alternative is allowed (`{a,}` matches `a` or nothing). A group with no top-level `,` (`{a}`, `{}`) stays literal, as in bash and minimatch. When the pattern's braces are not balanced, every `{` and `}` stays literal (today's escape). A `,` outside any group stays literal. The memo keyed on the raw pattern is unchanged. `globToRegex` is recorded at complexity 22 in `packages/nax/scripts/baselines/complexity-baseline.json` against the strict limit 20 (`packages/repo-tooling/scripts/check-complexity.ts`), and the ratchet fails a function whose score grows: the brace handling goes in new file-local helpers (finding the group extents, translating one group), each scoring 20 or less, so `globToRegex` itself does not grow; when its score drops, lower its baseline entry to the new score.

`classifyPattern(normalizedPattern)` (file-local, `rules-lint.ts:95`). Baseline: a segment is a wildcard segment only if it contains `*` or `?`. Target: a segment containing `{` also ends the literal prefix, so a brace pattern is never checked as a literal path. Update the doc comment above it, which says `{` and `}` are matched literally.

`SCOPE_GLOB_META = /[*?[{]/` — `scope-path-match/index.ts:43`; already treats `{` as glob syntax, unchanged.
`_rulesLintDeps.globHasMatch(pattern: string, cwd: string): GlobMatchResult` — `src/cli/rules-lint.ts:186` (in `_rulesLintDeps`, `:160`); `GlobMatchResult = "match" | "no-match" | "unknown"`.

**Scope** — In: shared matcher helpers, rules-lint classifier/comment, complexity baseline reduction when applicable and focused regex/runtime/lint tests. Out: Vitest include parsing (US-001), smart-test caps (US-003), config validation (US-004), reserved names (US-005), PID cleanup (US-006) and auto-PR (US-007). Brace expansion in the other glob converters (`src/utils/path-filters.ts`, `src/test-runners/conventions.ts`). They are separate matchers with their own callers. Extglob syntax (`?(x)`, `+(x)`, `@(x)`, `!(x)`) and character ranges in rule `appliesTo`. Only `{a,b}` groups are expanded. A runtime chunk scope path that contains a literal brace group with a comma (for example a file named `{a,b}.ts`). After US-002 it is read as a glob by attribution.

**Interface**
```ts
globToRegex(pattern: string): RegExp
ruleMatchesScopeFiles(appliesTo: string[] | undefined, scopeFiles: string[] | undefined): boolean
pathMatchesScope(scopePaths: string[], filePath: string): boolean
```
Keep all existing matcher exports and static-rules re-exports; add no public brace-parser API. Add `packages/nax/test/unit/context/engine/scope-path-match-braces.test.ts` for all brace, attribution and lint cases instead of extending the 783-line rules-lint.test.ts. Verify the complexity ratchet using bun run check:complexity; this is not a behavioral AC.

userStories.title: Escalate capped import-grep selection to the full suite
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix M17 by refusing partial import-grep results when the scan exceeds its cap.

**Motivation** — Repro: 261 test files that all import `src/a`; the fallback returned 200.

**Approach** — `importGrepFallback(sourceFiles, workdir, testFilePatterns, maxScanFiles = MAX_GREP_TEST_FILES): Promise<string[]>` (`smart-runner.ts:138`). Baseline: stops collecting at `maxScanFiles` files, logs at debug, greps the collected files. Target: when the scan yields a file past `maxScanFiles` (the scan holds more than `maxScanFiles` files), it reads no test file, logs one warn on the `smart-runner` stage naming the cap and that scoped selection escalates to the full suite, and returns `[]`. Exactly `maxScanFiles` files is not over the cap. `smart-runner.ts` is 599 lines, so the change must not grow it past the 600-line source limit (replace the debug block in place).

`selectScopedTests(input): Promise<SelectScopedTestsResult>` — `src/test-runners/scoped-selection.ts:98`; an empty Pass 2 result already returns its `fullSuite()` result.

**Scope** — In: cap overflow behavior/logging and tests proving the real fallback reaches full-suite selection. Out: Vitest parsing (US-001), scope globs (US-002), package validation (US-004), project names (US-005), PID cleanup (US-006) and branch protection (US-007). Raising or removing `execution.smartTestRunner.maxScanFiles`, or scanning test files in a stable order. Deduplicating test files that two `testFilePatterns` both match. Each match counts toward `maxScanFiles`, so overlapping patterns can escalate to the full suite sooner.

**Interface**
```ts
importGrepFallback(sourceFiles, workdir, testFilePatterns, maxScanFiles = MAX_GREP_TEST_FILES): Promise<string[]>
selectScopedTests(input): Promise<SelectScopedTestsResult>
```
Keep the existing return type and fullSuite fallback contract. Add `packages/nax/test/unit/verification/import-grep-fallback-cap.test.ts` for all new cases, including the cross-module seam, without changing existing tests. Stub _bunDeps.glob/file, capture stage-specific warnings, and leave _scopedSelectionDeps.importGrepFallback at its default real implementation for the selection seam. The existing cap tests assert only at most N reads and are regression guards, not sufficient fail-first tests. Verify smart-runner.ts remains <=600 lines with bun run check:file-sizes.

userStories.title: Validate hydrated package configs through shared preparation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix M19 by sharing package-layer preparation/final validation and making registry hydration resilient per package.

**Motivation** — Repro: `.nax/mono/packages/api/config.json` = `{"execution":{"costLimit":-5}}`; `loadConfigForWorkdir` throws `PER_PACKAGE_PROFILE_INVALID`, `loadPackageOverrideWithConfig` returns `costLimit: -5`.

**Approach** — `loadPackageOverrideWithConfig({ repoRoot, packageDir, rootConfig })` (`loader.ts:390`). Baseline: `mergePackageConfig(rootConfig, data.fields)`, profile layers, `mergePackageConfig` again, no validation. Target: the package fields go through the same per-layer preparation `loadConfigForWorkdir` runs (env resolution, compat shims, `rejectPipelineModeKeys`, `warnQualityCommandChains`, the legacy reject guards, `stripRemovedConfig`), and the merged, profile-overlaid result goes through the same final validation (legacy reject guards, `validatePermissionsBlock`, `stripRemovedConfig`, `NaxConfigSchema.safeParse`), with schema failures throwing `NaxError` code `PER_PACKAGE_PROFILE_INVALID` with the same message shape `loadConfigForWorkdir` uses; guard failures propagate their original error codes, including `CONFIG_PERMISSIONS_ALLOW_ALIAS_CONFLICT`. The returned `overlay` stays the declared package fields plus profile layers as today; the `review.commands` bridge stays and runs on the validated config. Both steps move into a new module `src/config/package-layer.ts` that `loadConfigForWorkdir` also calls, so the two paths cannot drift again; `loader.ts` (599 lines) must end at or under 599 lines.

The caller creates one `warnDedupe` per package resolution and passes it to both functions and to `loadPackageProfileLayers` (`loadPackageOverrideData` takes it as a parameter instead of creating its own, and returns `{ fields, layers, chain }` so the chain reaches `validatePackageConfig`). `resolveEnvVarsWarnOnFailure` (file-local in `loader.ts:70`, used by the root chain too) moves to `package-layer.ts` and is exported for `loader.ts`, so `package-layer.ts` never imports `loader.ts`. The interim `stripRemovedConfig(merged)` pass in `loadConfigForWorkdir` (`loader.ts:~528`) stays where it is.
`validatePackageConfig` owns only the guards, `validatePermissionsBlock`, the strip and `safeParse`; it does not call `applyWorkflowMode`. `loadConfigForWorkdir` keeps its own `pinRootOnlyKeysRaw`, `profile`/`profileChain` stamp, `applyWorkflowMode` and cache write around the call. `loadPackageOverrideWithConfig` keeps its second whitelist `mergePackageConfig(rootConfig, resolved)`, then applies `pinRootOnlyKeysRaw(merged, rootConfig, packageDir, warnDedupe.warn)` before `validatePackageConfig` (the same order as `loader.ts:554`, so a package's root-only `execution.*` value is warned about and dropped, never validated), then applies the `review.commands` bridge to the validated config; `hydrate` keeps its own `pinRootOnlyKeys` and `applyWorkflowMode`.

`createPackageRegistry().hydrate(packageDirs, loadOverride?)` (`runtime/packages.ts:210`). Baseline: the loop awaits each package in order, so the first rejection skips every later package and `hydrated` is never set. `run-setup.ts:300-314` catches the rejection and warns `Per-package config hydration failed — using root config`. Target: `hydrate` hydrates every package it can, sets `hydrated = true`, and then rejects with the first package's error when any package failed (later failures are logged at warn on the `packages` stage with their `packageDir`). A failed package is not hydrated and resolves to the root config. `run-setup.ts` is unchanged: it still warns and continues, now with the validation error in its `error` field.

Guard errors retain their original codes, including CONFIG_PERMISSIONS_ALLOW_ALIAS_CONFLICT from validatePermissionsBlock; the PER_PACKAGE_PROFILE_INVALID wrapper applies to schema safeParse failures, as required by AC4. An unset package environment variable uses the existing warn-and-keep behavior. Preserve the exact schema-error message shape: Per-package config <override or profile "chain"> produced an invalid config for package "<packageDir>": followed by newline-separated dotted-path errors, with stage config, packageDir and profileChain metadata.

**Scope** — In: new shared package-layer module, both package-resolution entry points, one dedupe per resolution, profile-chain plumbing, raw root-only pinning, review-command provenance and partial hydrate failure handling. Out: test parser/glob/cap fixes (US-001–US-003), reserved names (US-005), PID identity (US-006) and auto-PR (US-007). Validating `loadPackageOverride` (`loader.ts:384`), the declared-values reader the finish quality gate uses for command provenance. It keeps returning the declared fields unvalidated. Making an invalid package config fatal at run start. `run-setup` keeps its non-fatal catch, so the failed package runs on the root config after one warn carrying the validation error.

**Interface**
```ts
// Per-layer preparation of one package config.json's fields (profile key already removed).
export function preparePackageLayer(
  fields: Record<string, unknown>,
  packageDir: string,
  logger: Logger,
  warnDedupe: ConfigWarnDedupe,
): Record<string, unknown>; // env resolved, shimmed, legacy-guarded, removed keys stripped
// Final validation of the merged, profile-overlaid raw config. Returns Zod result.data.
export function validatePackageConfig(
  rawMerged: Record<string, unknown>,
  packageDir: string,
  profileChain: readonly string[],
  warnDedupe: ConfigWarnDedupe,
): NaxConfig; // throws NaxError PER_PACKAGE_PROFILE_INVALID
```
`createPackageRegistry(loader, repoRoot).hydrate(packageDirs, loadOverride?)` — `src/runtime/packages.ts:210`; with no `loadOverride` it calls `loadPackageOverrideWithConfig`.

Add package-override-validation.test.ts rather than extending the 732-line loader-legacy-shim.test.ts. Drive the new exported validatePackageConfig directly and the consumer seam through real hydrate with no loadOverride against a temp repo. Tests calling loadConfigForWorkdir isolate NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR, call _clearRootConfigCache and write root .nax/config.json as integration/runtime/package-profile-registry.test.ts:31-48 does; use initLogger/addSink logging assertions as loader-legacy-shim.test.ts:261-295 does. Exercise env and shim behavior through both entry points. Existing integration/runtime/package-profile-registry.test.ts must stay green without assertion changes. Verify typecheck and loader.ts <=599 lines as implementation gates, not behavioral ACs.

userStories.title: Reserve project names owned by nax global directories
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix M20 by making project-name validation reject collisions with nax-owned global subdirectories through one static list.

**Motivation** — `runs`, `profiles`, `acp`, `plugins`, `events` and `memory` all validate, and `nax migrate --reclaim profiles` renames `~/.nax/profiles` into `_archive` with no prompt, taking every named profile with it.

**Approach** — `validateProjectName(name)` (`init.ts:42`) and the `name` refine in `NaxConfigSchema` (`schemas.ts:103`). Baseline: both reserve the inline list `["global", "_archive"]`. Target: both read one exported constant `RESERVED_PROJECT_NAMES` in `src/config/paths/index.ts` (next to `globalConfigDir`) = `["global", "profiles", "runs", "events", "plugins", "acp", "memory", "hooks", "_archive"]` — every directory nax itself creates under `globalConfigDir()` (`runtime/paths.ts:37`, `config/profile.ts:83`, `utils/paths.ts:33`, `utils/paths.ts:40`, `cli/plugins.ts:25`, `agents/acp/open-context.ts:62`, `memory/paths.ts:115`, `cli/init.ts:291`, `commands/migrate.ts:64`). A doc comment on the constant lists these sites. `validateProjectName` keeps its reserved check before the `_` prefix check and returns `name '<name>' is reserved`; the schema refine's message names the rejected value. `migrateCommand` is unchanged: it already validates through `validateProjectName`.

**Scope** — In: the constant, init validation, schema refine and tests through migrate reclaim/merge. Out: package-layer validation (US-004), other gates fixes (US-001–US-003), PID signaling (US-006) and publication guards (US-007). An existing project already named one of the newly reserved names. Its `.nax/config.json` stops validating and must be renamed by hand; no migration is added. A repo with no `name` in its config whose directory is named like a reserved name. `getProjectKey` (`config/project-key.ts:25`) falls back to the directory's basename without `validateProjectName`, so it can still collide. `trust` from the review's M20 repro: nax writes `~/.nax/trust.json`, a file, so no directory collides; it is not reserved. Making nax's own path helpers (`profile.ts`, `utils/paths.ts`, `plugins.ts`, `memory/paths.ts`, `open-context.ts`) read their directory names from `RESERVED_PROJECT_NAMES`. The constant is a list for validation only. Making `nax migrate --reclaim` refuse a `~/.nax/<name>` directory that has no `.identity` file.

**Interface**
```ts
export const RESERVED_PROJECT_NAMES = ["global", "profiles", "runs", "events", "plugins", "acp", "memory", "hooks", "_archive"];
```

userStories.title: Signal snapshotted descendants after reparenting
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix M21 by identifying snapshotted processes by pid and start time rather than parent identity during both tree-kill passes.

**Motivation** — A descendant whose parent exits on SIGTERM is reparented (ppid 1), so its own SIGTERM (sent concurrently) and the SIGKILL pass both skip it and it outlives the run.

**Approach** — `signalIfUnchanged(proc, signal)` (private, `pid-registry.ts:328`). Baseline: skips when `parentPid` or `startedAt` differs from the snapshot. Target: skips only when `startedAt` differs (the PID was reused). A changed `parentPid` alone is signalled, for both `TERM` and `KILL`. The skip warn keeps its fields.

`PidRegistry.killAll()` — `src/execution/pid-registry.ts:153`; calls the private `killPidTree`, which signals TERM to every target concurrently, sleeps `PID_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS`, then signals KILL.

**Scope** — In: the private identity comparison and focused tests through killAll proving both passes, PID reuse and failed identity lookup behavior. Out: test selection/config/name fixes (US-001–US-005) and publishing (US-007). Killing a reparented descendant that was not in the snapshot `killPidTree` took before the TERM pass. Do not change process-group signaling, traversal, grace timing or existing PID safety guards.

**Interface**
```ts
signalIfUnchanged(proc, signal)
PidRegistry.killAll()
```
Keep signalIfUnchanged private and preserve existing warn data including expectedParentPid, currentParentPid, expectedStartedAt and currentStartedAt. Add pid-registry-reparent.test.ts rather than growing the 640-line pid-registry.test.ts. Stub _pidRegistryDeps.spawn and sleep, never kill real processes. A changed start time still skips with the existing warning; failed per-pid ps lookup still sends no signal.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] killAll() with a registered root whose ps -eo snapshot lists a descendant D (ppid = the root's child C), where the per-pid ps -o lookup for D returns ppid 1 and the snapshot's start time, sends kill -TERM D.
[unit] In the same reparented-D case, killAll() also sends kill -KILL D.
[unit] killAll() where the per-pid lookup for D returns ppid 1 and the snapshot's start time only after the TERM pass (its first lookup returns the snapshot ppid), sends kill -KILL D.
[unit] killAll() where the per-pid lookup for D returns the snapshot ppid and a different start time does not send kill -TERM D or kill -KILL D.

[unit] In the changed-start-time case, exactly one of the warns logged on the pid-registry stage has a message starting Skipping SIGTERM for PID, and its data carries expectedStartedAt and currentStartedAt.
[unit] killAll() where the per-pid lookup for D fails (non-zero exit) sends no signal to D.

userStories.title: Block auto-PR publication from protected branches
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Fix M22 by applying the publisher's static and remote-default branch protection to both auto-PR entry points.

**Motivation** — `autoPrPlugin` (`src/plugins/builtin/auto-pr/index.ts`) runs `git push -u origin <context.branch>` and opens a PR for whatever branch the run was on.

**Approach** — `isPublishableBranch(branch, defaultBranch?)` (`workflow/finalize.ts:75`, with `PROTECTED_BRANCHES`). Target: moves to `src/utils/git.ts` unchanged; `finalize.ts` imports it from there and keeps re-exporting it, so its existing importers (`test/unit/workflow/finalize.test.ts`, `publish-protection.test.ts`) keep working. A plugin must not import from `src/workflow/`.

`_autoPrDeps` and `autoPrPlugin` (`src/plugins/builtin/auto-pr/index.ts`). Target: `_autoPrDeps` gains `readDefaultBranch(workdir: string): Promise<string | undefined>`, whose default runs `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` through `_autoPrDeps.run` (the hardened runner; the literal argv carries the file's `nax-git-env-allow` annotation, as `GIT_REMOTE_CMD` does) and strips `origin/`, returning `undefined` on a non-zero exit, an empty answer or a throw. `shouldRun` returns `false` after the `enabled` and story-summary checks and before any remote or forge lookup when `isPublishableBranch(context.branch, await _autoPrDeps.readDefaultBranch(context.workdir))` is false, logging one warn naming the branch. `execute` makes the same check first and returns `{ success: false, message }` naming the branch without running `git push`.

Default-branch lookup fails: treated as unknown: only `""`, `main` and `master` are protected.

**Scope** — In: relocate/re-export the shared predicate, add injectable default-branch lookup with hardened runner, protect shouldRun and execute, add focused protected-branch tests, and update dependency snapshots in two existing test files. Out: workflow publish policy redesign, all other fixes (US-001–US-006). US-007 only: a branch protection list configured by the user. Only `""`, `main`, `master` and the remote default branch are protected, as in the workflow publisher. Preserve timeout, draft/forge behavior and the existing post-push duplicate-PR recheck. Do not import workflow/git.ts from the plugin.

**Interface**
```ts
isPublishableBranch(branch, defaultBranch?)
readDefaultBranch(workdir: string): Promise<string | undefined>
```
The moved predicate retains its existing TypeScript signature `export function isPublishableBranch(branch: string, defaultBranch?: string): boolean`. Its unchanged protected set is ["", "main", "master"], with branch !== defaultBranch as the additional predicate.

Add auto-pr-protected-branch.test.ts for the new cases. The readDefaultBranch seam's consumers are shouldRun and execute; test both with explicit stubs and exercise the default implementation by stubbing only _autoPrDeps.run.

Vitest `test.projects` / workspace entries and an `alias` or other object holding a `test:` key before the config's own `test` block. Only the first `test: {` block's top-level `include` is read.
US-007 only: a branch protection list configured by the user. Only `""`, `main`, `master` and the remote default branch are protected, as in the workflow publisher.
